review_state: AI self-reviewed synthesis of retained dated evidence

records.title: Southwest semiconductor corridor: follow water through the receiving system
records.answer: A fab announcement, a wastewater authorization and a regional resource account answer different questions. The retained Phoenix and TSMC records describe dependencies and unresolved acceptance evidence, not a corridor-wide operating result.
records.scope: The existing multi-state U.S. Southwest semiconductor corridor, centred here on Arizona's named wastewater example. It is not the TSMC campus, Phoenix municipality or one uniform utility territory.

related.title: TSMC Arizona campus and individual asset boundaries

sections.heading: Keep the regional boundary visible
sections.text: This corridor connects industrial sites with water providers, electricity networks, workers and suppliers. Its existing geography includes Arizona and adjacent Southwest industrial regions; the Phoenix wastewater example covers a narrower municipal relationship. The same source cannot establish capacity across all those boundaries. Read the project-specific account alongside this regional synthesis, and identify the service provider and receiving asset before transferring an observation beyond the campus.

sections.heading: Authorization starts a delivery chain
sections.text: The retained May 20 Council results record adoption of Item 73. The accompanying proposal concerns new force and gravity lines and two lift-station improvements. Increased acceptance is conditional on completion, and the initial Industrial Reclamation Water Plant deadline is June 30, 2028. These instruments establish an authorized path and future requirements. They do not certify that the receiving network, treatment assets and every connecting work have been commissioned together.

sections.heading: A corporate report does not settle commissioning
sections.text: The November 21 review preserves a tension in TSMC's 2025 environmental report: Arizona prose describes construction starting in 2025 and a planned discharge capability, while a diagram uses a built-plant label. The water and discharge charts pool Arizona with other subsidiaries. Neither the wording tension nor those pooled metrics provides a dated Arizona commissioning instrument or a facility-only water balance. Keep the ambiguity visible instead of selecting the more advanced label.

sections.heading: Financial shares are not physical flows
sections.text: Phoenix's retained disclosure attributes 1.331% of wastewater rate revenue to TSMC for fiscal 2024–25. The disclosure was revised in January 2026 and predates the May authorization. A revenue share reflects a financial measure, not a share of wastewater volume. Multiplying citywide flows by that percentage would invent a facility return. Water demand, pollutant loading, treatment cost and billed revenue require their own units, periods and accounting boundaries.

sections.heading: Acceptance needs a completed project record
sections.text: The retained City requirements identify as-builts, certification and witnessed tests. The accompanying engineer certificate has blank project and completion fields; it is a template, not proof that TSMC's works passed. These documents explain what an acceptance record should contain. The November 21 text inspection did not establish visual or signature verification, and failure to retrieve a completed instrument does not establish that no such instrument exists.

sections.heading: The regional question is how dependencies join
sections.text: A stronger corridor account would connect each named fab to accepted water and power service, then to compatible operating returns. Workforce completion and supplier capability need separate evidence, not an inference from announced investment or municipal authorization. The wastewater gate remains a project-specific checkpoint. It cannot decide every site's resource position, environmental performance or economic contribution, and this place synthesis creates no new stage or efficiency score.

next_artifacts: Named completed-and-accepted conveyance and reclamation instruments, with the receiving authority and asset boundary.
Arizona-only dated flow, compliance and water-balance records; preserve the distinctions between allocation, capacity, billed revenue and observed use.
Separate facility service and workforce/supplier evidence before making a corridor-wide operating claim.

records.title: Hanford waste treatment: connect the process to its receiving assets
records.answer: The retained September reports add operating quantities and receiving-system context. They do not turn DFLAW milestones into a complete Hanford material balance or a site-wide cleanup outcome.
records.scope: The Hanford site waste-treatment system in Washington, not all Washington State, a municipality, the entire cleanup mission or a single DFLAW treatment train.

related.title: DFLAW process account and dated material evidence

sections.heading: A site account contains several process boundaries
sections.text: Hanford's place account must connect treatment, supporting facilities, effluent handling, inventories and disposal without assigning one operating stage to the whole site. The retained monthly report separates LAW, balance-of-facilities and laboratory reporting. Those divisions are useful evidence boundaries, not interchangeable production totals. A milestone within DFLAW therefore belongs to its identified stream and facility before it can support a wider claim about the receiving system.

sections.heading: Keep monthly and cumulative quantities apart
sections.text: The retained September report states 40,575.5 gallons of feed during the month and 230,900 gallons cumulatively through September 30. It also reports a September 20 daily glass maximum of 9.76 metric tons. Monthly feed, cumulative feed and a peak daily output describe different intervals and units. Dividing or combining them would not yield a defensible production efficiency or an accepted recurring rate.

sections.heading: Movement is not disposal acceptance
sections.text: The same report describes 165 containers shipped to the Integrated Disposal Facility by September 30. That is a shipment count, not a common-period accepted glass mass. A receiving-system account needs the batch, dispatch record, recipient and actual acceptance status. It should also distinguish the primary immobilized product from secondary waste sent elsewhere for treatment; the inspected offsite grouting passage was qualitative rather than a compatible numerical balance.

sections.heading: Inventory context is useful but incomplete
sections.text: The inspected material includes cumulative effluent exceeding 3.7 million gallons and separate LERF inventory context in the related TPA report. The latter table's screenshot failed, and no table numbers were adopted from text extraction. A facility inventory snapshot can help identify a missing join without supplying all process inventories or their change over a common period. It would be equally misleading to call all inventory evidence absent or to treat the snapshot as a reconciled balance.

sections.heading: Observation and publication dates serve different purposes
sections.text: The consent report covers September 1–30 and was placed online October 28; its November meeting label is not the observation period. The separate third-quarter accession covers July–September, identifies 162 pages and records online availability on November 9. The November 21 download attempts timed out, so the review established metadata rather than the quarterly report's contents. Keep that access limit alongside the monthly evidence without inferring that the quarterly artifact does not exist.

sections.heading: Reconcile the same system over the same interval
sections.text: A reproducible account would join feed, accepted glass, secondary waste, inventory changes, losses and adjustments using compatible units and a stated reconciliation method. It would identify estimates and uncertainty and tie receiving decisions to the correct material. The saved November decision retains the material-balance signal In Review. This narrative makes the site's dependencies easier to follow; it does not resolve that gate or score the wider cleanup mission.

next_artifacts: A completed-period reconciliation with compatible process inputs, outputs, inventory changes, losses, adjustments and uncertainty.
Named downstream acceptance records linked to the relevant batches and receiving facilities.
Readable official third-quarter report content, assessed within its actual scope rather than treated as a substitute for the required balance.

records.title: Space Coast: separate site authority from a working launch corridor
records.answer: The retained FAA instrument establishes a specific Shuttle Landing Facility site-authority account. It does not establish vehicle permission, mission performance or reliable capacity across the wider Space Coast system.
records.scope: Kennedy Space Center, Cape Canaveral Space Force Station and connected Florida Space Coast systems. The Shuttle Landing Facility is one asset within that regional account, not the whole corridor.
records.context_role: Shuttle Landing Facility companion review only

sections.heading: The corridor is not one licensed object
sections.text: A multi-user space corridor combines federal facilities, launch and reentry sites, shared infrastructure and supporting local systems. This place identity organizes those relationships; it is not one project and has no single place-level conversion stage. A licence for one site cannot establish the authority or readiness of neighbouring sites. The retained FAA inventory is therefore a navigation aid whose individual entries must still be matched to their exact instruments.

sections.heading: Retain the actual renewal dates
sections.text: The September 15 inspection retrieved LRSO 18-018 Revision 2 for Space Florida at the Shuttle Landing Facility. It was issued January 8, 2026, became effective January 15, 2026 and expires January 15, 2031. September 15 is the retrieval date, not the issue date. The saved inspection covered the three-page licence and Order A-1; it did not independently validate the digital signature or supply a new legal acceptance decision.

sections.heading: Later access failure does not erase that instrument
sections.text: On November 21 the exact linked FAA DRS surface returned no readable text. The follow-up is consequently a bounded access blocker, not fresh confirmation of the instrument's disposition. The explanatory page and inventory still showed older dates. Their stale expiry wording cannot, by itself, revoke the retained renewal. Likewise, the inventory's November 18 update is a whole-page date, not proof that its SLF row was newly reviewed.

sections.heading: Site authority and operation remain separate
sections.text: The renewal establishes the retained site-authority account. It does not establish a vehicle licence, completed Coast Guard agreement, an accepted capital asset, a flown mission or recurring service. Those objects have different issuers and recipients. A useful operating chain joins the exact site, vehicle and mission records with any required conditions and actual performance; it cannot skip those joins by treating a site licence as a general readiness certificate.

sections.heading: Regional capacity needs regional receiving evidence
sections.text: Range availability, utility resilience, access infrastructure and workforce conditions affect the corridor but are not measured by a site licence. A place-wide reliability or local-benefit claim would need its own defined assets, periods and denominators. Preserve the individual project accounts and investigate those dependencies separately. A regional narrative can explain why a join matters without assigning the same condition or outcome to every launch, reentry or supporting facility.

sections.heading: Keep the next review bounded to its purpose
sections.text: The saved November companion asks for the exact current FAA instrument and any later formal disposition or explicit condition-compliance evidence. Its next editorial checkpoint is an access and review appointment, not an expiry forecast. Until an exact artifact changes the account, retain both the September renewal inspection and November blocker. A later mission or infrastructure assertion still needs its own evidence rather than inheriting approval from this place reading.

next_artifacts: An authorized readable copy of the exact FAA instrument and any later formal amendment or disposition.
Separate explicit condition-compliance, vehicle/mission and accepted-asset records for any operating claim.
Defined regional service, utility, access and workforce observations before drawing place-wide performance or benefit conclusions.

records.title: Northern Virginia: distinguish policy from delivered data-center service
records.answer: Loudoun's reported limited application pause and proposed Phase 2 standards are different policy objects. Neither establishes a named facility's power service, permit compliance or performance across the Northern Virginia corridor.
records.scope: The existing Northern Virginia data-center corridor across Loudoun, Prince William and Fairfax counties. Loudoun-only policy does not become a rule for every county, utility territory or customer in this regional account.
records.context_role: Related Loudoun policy watch only; no project appointment reset

related.title: Golden-Mars transmission and separate GS-5 tariff context

sections.heading: Match each authority to its geography
sections.text: The corridor spans several counties and overlapping service systems. Land-use policy, transmission authority, tariff terms, water service and actual customer operation do not share one decision boundary. The Loudoun page concerns that county's proposed amendments; it is not a regional permit or a finding about every data center. Keep the existing Golden-Mars and GS-5 project/context account separate from this place narrative and from other counties' obligations.

sections.heading: A reported pause has several distinct dates
sections.text: The county's November 18 announcement reports a November 17 Board decision to pause certain legislative data-center and substation applications, with a stated September 15 effective date. The saved review inspected that announcement on November 21. These dates describe publication, reported action, reported effectiveness and inspection respectively. The announcement supports the county's stated account; the review did not independently inspect the adopted resolution or decide how it applies to a named project.

sections.heading: Proposed standards remain a different object
sections.text: The retained project page still labels its Phase 2 amendment texts proposed. Its public-comment section points to a December 1 Board packet. The September proposal summary identifies CPAM-2025-0001 and ZOAM-2025-0002; the recorded inspection covered introductory text, not a complete technical review or an enacted instrument. A limited application pause does not transform that separate standards proposal into adopted law, and a future meeting reference does not establish an actual disposition.

sections.heading: The exact instrument remains an access gap
sections.text: The announcement's exact November 17 staff-report link returned 403 in the saved review. No report or resolution body was obtained through that surface. That limitation is narrower than saying no instrument exists, and it does not invalidate the inspected announcement. Resolve the precise instrument and its scope before making a condition-compliance or project-permission claim. No browser workaround, access change or inferred permit decision is part of this place synthesis.

sections.heading: A customer connection is a separate evidence chain
sections.text: A regional demand statement or policy action does not identify which customer receives accepted service. A useful place account follows the named facility through relevant land decisions, infrastructure works, inspection, energization and the service arrangement, then examines compatible operating returns. Water use, noise, reliability and costs require their own observations. These are evidence requirements for a receiving-system account, not findings that any particular customer has failed to meet them.

sections.heading: Policy appointments cannot reschedule project obligations
sections.text: The saved Loudoun watch calls for a bounded check after the announced December 1 packet. That policy appointment does not reset Golden-Mars, GS-5 or qualification-file dates. Keep the proposed standards, reported pause and named-project decisions separately addressable. A future adopted text may change the policy account; it still cannot, by itself, establish constructed infrastructure, delivered capacity or a corridor-wide affordability result.

next_artifacts: The actual Phase 2 Board packet and disposition, with adopted text and effective dates only if established.
The exact limited-pause resolution and its scope, without transferring it to unrelated counties or project obligations.
Separate named service, infrastructure acceptance and operating evidence before asserting capacity, reliability or community outcomes.

records.title: Louisiana broadband: follow each service cohort into adoption
records.answer: Louisiana's broadband program contains different provider and funding populations. The retained records describe a Nextlink service area, Starlink's planned grant scope and a later supplemental eligibility process; none supplies a common observed adoption rate.
records.scope: The existing statewide Louisiana broadband system, with two separately governed provider examples. A tower in Bienville, its Bossier service area, a Vermilion Parish offer and statewide eligible locations are not the same geography or population.

related_cycle_contexts.label: Separate Starlink adoption companion
related_cycle_contexts.relation: Related through the retained Louisiana Atlas relationship, not an assigned place-page receipt or a new cycle decision.

sections.heading: Start with the service cohort
sections.text: A useful Louisiana account follows the people and locations to which a particular service offer applies. Statewide grants describe a delivery program; a tower describes infrastructure; an eligible-location list describes the addresses included in a funding or coverage population. These are different starting points for measuring adoption. The state portrait therefore keeps Nextlink and Starlink separate and asks how a fixed group moved from service availability to installation, subscription and use. Program-level progress should not be inferred by adding unlike provider counts.

sections.heading: Nextlink activation and the Bossier service area
sections.text: The state and provider releases are dated May 13, 2026 and describe a May 1 activation. The tower is in southern Bienville, while the stated 104-location service area is in Bossier. The infrastructure location and the customer population must remain distinct. Availability for those locations is a meaningful delivery milestone, but the retained releases do not provide a measured subscriber numerator, observation period and method for that same cohort. Nextlink's company-wide subscriber total and wider sector goals cannot be divided by 104 to produce a Louisiana take rate.

sections.heading: Starlink grant scope and the separate local offer
sections.text: The June 11 grant announcement describes a planned 10,635-location scope and a prospective end-of-summer timetable. The later passage in the August 25 economic-development announcement describes a Vermilion Parish discount and hardware offer. Those records concern different populations and stages: a grant's intended reach is not the number of households that accepted an offer. Passing the forecast date does not establish completed installation. The November 21 companion review retained the adoption question as In Review; it did not turn a promotional offer or the separate spaceport proposal into broadband performance.

sections.heading: The supplemental round does not replace either denominator
sections.text: The November 18 announcement identifies approximately 18,431 potentially eligible supplemental locations and a January 2, 2027 challenge deadline, followed by further authorization steps. This is a prospective eligibility process, not an observed customer return. Its location total must not replace the 104-location Nextlink cohort or the planned 10,635-location Starlink scope. The resource library also lists GUMBO 1.0 performance reports alongside GUMBO 2.0 materials. A report under one funding program cannot be treated as the other program's provider return merely because both appear in the same library.

sections.heading: What the retained access limits leave unresolved
sections.text: The November review recovered only a JavaScript-required notice from the Starlink support route, and the progress PDF response exceeded the reader's size limit. Its text, pages and totals were not inspected. Two ConnectLA article bodies—the partnership-recognition item and the construction forecast—also remained inaccessible. Their index titles are discovery context, not fresh article-body evidence. These limits leave the exact adoption question open; they do not establish zero customers or the absence of a completed return. Earlier observations remain dated history rather than replacements for the failed November inspections.

sections.heading: An adoption account needs a stable population and period
sections.text: A decisive return would identify the provider, fixed eligible-location cohort, service-availability date, reporting period and method used to count installed or subscribed locations. The numerator and denominator must refer to that same population. Counts of accounts, installations and occupied locations should not be interchanged without an explicit definition, and a later cohort revision should preserve the earlier version. These are the requirements for interpreting the next return, not measured results. The separate Starlink companion and Nextlink gate keep their own December 21 editorial checkpoints; neither date predicts an agency publication.

next_artifacts: A provider- or ConnectLA-issued completed-period return for the fixed Bossier service cohort, with an observed numerator, matching eligible-location denominator and counting method.
A separate Starlink installation or subscription return identifying the retained Louisiana BEAD cohort; do not substitute a discount, global total or supplemental-round list.
A documented cohort version and service-availability basis that permit comparison across periods without merging provider or funding populations.

records.title: Montana broadband: connect the reporting rules to a completed project quarter
records.answer: Montana's retained guidance distinguishes construction, serviceability, active subscribers and payment controls. The missing link in this bounded account is a completed BEAD project-quarter return with an identified location cohort—not another reporting instruction or an ARPA announcement.
records.scope: The existing Montana statewide broadband-delivery system. The place is distinct from its thirty-two proposal project identities, and the shared ConnectMT administration does not merge BEAD and ARPA funding or terrestrial and satellite reporting populations.

sections.heading: Read the state system through exact project quarters
sections.text: Montana's statewide portrait is a way to follow delivery across projects, not a thirty-third proposal project or a combined project-and-place total. A useful result must name the project, reporting period, location cohort and completion state. The November 21 review found updated reporting guidance and a post-award navigation guide, but did not retrieve the exact qualifying completed BEAD project-quarter report. This leaves the result unverified in that inspection; it does not establish that no project work occurred or that every project has zero subscribers.

sections.heading: Terrestrial progress has several distinct measures
sections.text: The September terrestrial instructions request project finances, progress, active subscribers, and locations constructed and made serviceable during the reporting period. The FAQ separately discusses estimated overall work, serviceable locations and active users, and permits an empty served-location attachment under specified conditions. Each field answers a different question. A construction estimate is not an active-user count, and an empty attachment is not evidence of zero construction. The report must retain the field definition and its period before any statewide summary can compare projects.

sections.heading: Satellite subscriber stock is not equipment shipment flow
sections.text: The June LEO instructions distinguish subscribers at period end from customer-premises-equipment shipments during the period. They also tie the reporting window to availability certification. Period-end subscriber stock and period shipment flow cannot be substituted for one another or added into a single adoption measure. A construction field marked not applicable for a satellite service does not demonstrate terrestrial completion. The required next evidence is the filled return and its certification basis; the reporting contract alone is not observed customer uptake.

sections.heading: Disbursement controls and portal guidance are different artifacts
sections.text: Version 6.0 of the disbursement guide is dated September 2026. The inspected sections describe network-activation documentation, LEO installments, reporting and approval. Those prescribed conditions are not proof that a payment or asset acceptance occurred. The separate post-award guide explains navigation and export of an ARPA/BEAD status view; no account was entered and no report exported in the retained review. The screenshot requests failed, so the embedded interface examples are not described as visually inspected or as blank completed reports.

sections.heading: Cascade County does not answer the BEAD quarter question
sections.text: The September 24 Cascade County announcement explicitly identifies ConnectMT ARPA support for the Spectrum expansion. BEAD appears as separate background. This is useful context for the state's broader broadband system, but it cannot serve as the required BEAD project-quarter return. Nor can locations passed be relabelled active subscriptions. Keeping the funding identifier attached to each result prevents a real delivery announcement in one program from silently closing an unresolved evidence question in another.

sections.heading: Build a comparable state account from complete returns
sections.text: The next usable return should carry one exact BEAD project ID, the quarter's dates, its location cohort, observed completion state, outcome denominator and method. Terrestrial construction and serviceability fields should remain separate from the LEO subscriber and shipment fields. A later state summary can describe which populations are comparable and which are not, rather than manufacturing a blended completion percentage. The December 21 appointment is the saved editorial checkpoint for seeking that evidence. It does not redate the thirty-two proposal dossiers or promote their independent project stages.

next_artifacts: One official completed BEAD project-quarter report with project identity, reporting dates, location cohort, completion state and an observed outcome denominator.
Definitions and period boundaries that distinguish terrestrial constructed/serviceable locations from LEO subscriber stock and equipment shipment flow.
Where a result claims payment, certification or acceptance, the corresponding exact approval artifact rather than its instructions or portal navigation guide.

records.title: Amtrak accessibility: distinguish deployment, closeout and reliable use
records.answer: Amtrak's national accessibility account connects several kinds of progress without turning them into one result. Installed passenger information, final program closeout and repeated performance of a named asset require different evidence and reporting populations.
records.scope: Retained national rail-network context, excluded from the eligible-place target because an operator's network is not one local place. Named stations and corridors need their own geographic scope; this reading does not create or count them.

assigned_cycle_contexts.label: Independent named-asset reliability gate
assigned_cycle_contexts.relation: Assigned to this context route, but independent of PIDS closeout; its October inspection and November appointment are retained.

sections.heading: A national account is not one station or one outcome
sections.text: This account compares Amtrak's network-level accessibility reporting; it does not count the national network as a local place. Passenger Information Display Systems, or PIDS, are one part of that reporting. An installation inventory describes deployment, a final closeout record addresses the defined program's acceptance, and a named-asset reliability series describes operation over time. A station or corridor reading must keep its own boundary rather than inherit the national totals. The retained reports provide context for those questions, not a single combined accessibility score.

sections.heading: Keep the two installation counts in their reporting windows
sections.text: The June ADA report covers November 1, 2025 through April 30, 2026. Its inspected text describes performance ending March 31, closeout pending review with a May 31 target, and a table of 93 deployments. The June 1 accessibility progress report covers May 1, 2025 through April 30, 2026 and describes 117 installations, with financial closeout pending and a May 31 target. These are different report scopes and windows. The 93 and 117 counts must not be reconciled by assumption, and neither target date is evidence that acceptance actually occurred.

sections.heading: Closeout needs its own acceptance record
sections.text: The November 21 inspection retrieved historical report language, not a new November declaration of closeout status. The Federal Railroad Administration library route returned 404, while the linked grant-page request returned Cache miss. Those failures do not prove that a closeout record does not exist. The newly linked ten-page 2026–2028 accessibility plan is another distinct artifact: its cover and opening sections were inspected, and an exact PIDS text search returned no match. A future plan or an elapsed target cannot substitute for final acceptance tied to the same program scope and completed denominator.

sections.heading: Aggregate accessibility progress is not asset reliability
sections.text: The October 28 reliability review used the June annual reporting window, not October operating observations. Its aggregate station-compliance and remediation information does not identify repeated performance for one stable accessibility asset. Asset uptime, a failure rate and repair performance need a defined identity, observation period, exposure or denominator, failure definition and repair outcomes. This is why the reliability question remains independent of financial closeout: even an accepted deployment inventory would not supply the missing time series. The retained PDF review was text-only because image rendering failed.

sections.heading: Washington construction concerns a different asset population
sections.text: The October 26 announcement reports completed Washington track and tunnel upgrades and resumed service. That is a construction milestone for the population described in the release. Anticipated reliability benefits cannot be transferred into measured performance of station accessibility equipment, passenger information displays or another unnamed asset. The national reading can place these activities alongside one another, but it must keep their asset identities and outcome definitions separate rather than turn a shared operator name into a shared denominator.

sections.heading: What a named station account should add
sections.text: A useful next station or corridor account would connect the specific accessible asset to its responsible scope, service period, observed failures and repairs. It should show which facilities and passengers the record covers and which remain outside it. The next PIDS evidence instead is final accepted closeout for the defined deployment program. Those are separate requests, with saved checkpoints of November 25 for named-asset reliability and December 21 for closeout. They are editorial appointments, not expected publication dates, and this synthesis does not perform either future inspection.

next_artifacts: A final FRA-accepted PIDS closeout artifact tied to the exact program scope, completed deployment denominator and accountable acceptance decision.
A separate repeated named-accessibility-asset record with stable identity, reporting period, exposure or denominator, failure definition and repair outcomes.
A separately scoped station or corridor dossier connecting those records to a geographic place, without importing national totals as local performance.

records.title: NNSA two-site context: distinguish governance, capacity acceptance and reported output
records.answer: The retained public records answer three different administrative questions: whether enterprise cost and schedule recommendations are closed, whether operating capacity is accepted, and whether comparable recurring output is reported. None can be inferred solely from a first-unit milestone.
records.scope: Retained program context linking Los Alamos and Savannah River, not one geographic place. The parent is excluded from the eligible-place target; the two disconnected locations require separate local dossiers. This reading concerns public administrative status, not technical production methods.
records.context_role: Independent enterprise cost and schedule gate only

assigned_cycle_contexts.label: Independent accepted-capacity gate
assigned_cycle_contexts.relation: Assigned to this context route, but independent of enterprise baseline closure, first-unit qualification and recurring output.

assigned_cycle_contexts.label: Independent recurring-output gate
assigned_cycle_contexts.relation: Assigned to this context route, but independent of accepted capacity and enterprise baseline closure; its October inspection is retained.

sections.heading: Two sites require separate places and separate decisions
sections.text: The National Nuclear Security Administration's two-site program relates Los Alamos and Savannah River, but that relationship does not make one geographic place. This parent remains context only and contributes zero to the eligible-place target. Its public administrative account separates enterprise planning, accepted operating capacity and recurring qualified output. A project-level approval, a unit milestone or a program target cannot silently settle all three questions. The reading compares their dated evidence without promoting either site's stage or assessing technical production methods.

sections.heading: The exact GAO recommendations remain distinct
sections.text: In the November 21 inspection, GAO-23-104661 recommendation 1, concerning the life-cycle cost estimate, displayed Open. GAO-20-703 recommendation 3, concerning the integrated master schedule, also displayed Open. The latest explicit narrative inspected for each was April 2026; it was not a new November disposition. The expected December estimate and fiscal-year-end schedule timing are forecasts, not completed acceptance. Closure of recommendations 1, 2 or 4 in the latter report must not be transferred to recommendation 3. Original publication, later narrative and inspection dates keep different meanings.

sections.heading: Portfolio and priority counts do not close those recommendations
sections.text: The February 26, 2026 major-project product page describes a 28-project portfolio using June 2025 data. Its HTML summary was inspected, not the linked PDF anew. The July priority product describes 24 priority recommendations and five implemented recommendations; those aggregate counts do not identify closure of the two exact enterprise-baseline items. The inspected opening page of the priority letter retains cost-estimate needs. It is one page, not a review of the full five-page document, and its failed screenshot does not supply visual or signature verification.

sections.heading: A first qualified unit is a dated milestone, not accepted capacity
sections.text: The dated announcement was published October 2, 2024 and reports the first qualified unit achieved October 1, 2024, alongside continuing capacity work. It is not an October or November 2026 production event. The undated overview's older research-only wording does not negate that dated milestone. At the same time, the milestone is not a final operating-capacity acceptance instrument and does not establish recurring comparable output. The November 21 accepted-capacity review retained those distinctions; the public account does not infer that unavailable acceptance evidence means no activity occurred.

sections.heading: Draft environmental review is another decision process
sections.text: The retained index lists draft environmental-review materials and a July 16, 2026 comment deadline. The article is dated April 10, linked volume and summary entries carry April 8, and the cover uses the month April. These dates are not interchangeable. Only the cover and administrative cover sheet of the 259-page draft volume were read; neither the full technical document nor inspectable page images were reviewed. A draft, a document index or an elapsed comment deadline does not establish final operating-capacity acceptance.

sections.heading: Recurring output needs a separate comparable return
sections.text: The October 28 recurring-output review inspected the dated first-unit announcement and the undated overview, but did not retrieve the required recurring series. A public return would need a compatible acceptance definition, facility identity, reporting period and denominator before periods could be compared. This is an administrative evidence requirement, not a production-rate calculation or technical assessment. Its saved November 25 checkpoint remains separate from the December 21 baseline and accepted-capacity follow-ups. No Phase 61 named file is assigned to the accepted-capacity or recurring-output gates, and this synthesis creates none.

next_artifacts: The final enterprise cost estimate and integrated schedule with exact GAO closure evidence for recommendation 1 of GAO-23-104661 and recommendation 3 of GAO-20-703.
A separate final accountable operating-capacity acceptance instrument identifying its scope, responsible authority, dates and acceptance conditions.
A public recurring qualified-output return with compatible facility identity, acceptance definition, reporting period and denominator, kept separate from a first-unit announcement.
